reviewType: Actual view_image inspection of eight original PNGs only

images.observation: Header, instruction, three card names/costs and footer fit the window; no global HUD covers the discovery title. Unselected confirm is visibly disabled.
Blooddrinker is visibly selected with an opaque gold rectangular backing. It is a filled backing rather than a thin outline, but does not hide the card name, rules or footer.

Discovery overlay and selection backing are gone; battle HUD and the acquired Blooddrinker hand card are visible. The controlled foe is a white fixture rectangle; natural foe art is outside this review.
Six choices appear in a three-column/two-row layout. The initial viewport clips the lower part of the second row; the fixed footer remains clear. This image alone does not prove lower-row reading.

After scrolling, the full lower row and sixth Mana Surge card are visible, with its 2-cost tag, complete rules and selected gold backing. Upper-row clipping is confined to the scroll viewport; header and footer remain clear.

Hand visibly distinguishes a normal 1-cost Fireball, the transforming Broken Arrow label, and a temporary 0-cost Fireball. Cards overlap in the hand fan and extend below the viewport; this is not a full-card reading image.
Five separate consumed cards are visible. Normal and temporary same-name Fireballs remain distinct, with readable 0/1 costs and temporary badges. Title, total and return control are clear.
The enlarged Fireball shows its green 0-cost tag, temporary badge, name and complete short rule text. 2/5 navigation, close and battle-return controls fit without covering the enlarged card.

nonBlockingNotes: Selected discovery cards have an opaque gold rectangular backing, not a thin outline.
The expanded initial viewport clips the second row; the separately inspected scrolled image shows the full lower row.
White foe rectangles and the source-status probe card are controlled QA fixture content.
scope: Only these eight PNGs from player-1 at their actual 2560x1440 window were inspected.
No other size, DPI, animation, input routing, payment/RNG, cancellation, old callback, audio, performance or natural-foe coverage is claimed from images.
Native behavior receipts and the final player process status remain separate evidence.
